![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14223529/assets/963f8812eb8226617c7d893ebdf675747ebed12c92fc6369de2b153a1c2e3b58.png)

Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y,$ where $C$ is the path along the semicircle of radius $2,$ transversed from the point $(1,-2)$ to the point $(1,2),$ as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $y$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $y$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y={y}_{2}-{y}_{1},
$$

where ${y}_{2}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${y}_{1}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, ${y}_{2}=2$ and ${y}_{1}=-2.$ Therefore,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}y={y}_{2}-{y}_{1}=2-(-2)=4.
$$
